papers.title: Growth and reproductive responses of goat bucks to range grazing and concentrate-based production systems.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the effects of range grazing and three concentrate-based production systems on the growth, sexual behavior, scrotal circumference, and semen quality of breeding bucks. A total of 40 yearling bucks (10 bucks/treatment) were randomly allocated to range grazing (T1) and three different roughage-to-concentrate ratios: 60:40% (T2), 50:50% (T3), and 40:60% (T4) on a DM basis for a period of 90 days. All data were analyzed via ANOVA in SAS-JMP Pro 19. Bucks in T3 and T4 presented greater average daily gains (ADG) than those in T1 and T2 did, although T2 presented better gains than did T1. In T1 bucks, scrotal development, the number of mounts, the frequency of ejaculation, the courtship behavior score, and the testosterone concentration were lower, whereas the reaction time and refractory period were greater than those in T3 and T4. Bucks fed the T4 diet presented greater semen volume, followed by those fed T3 and T2, and the lowest semen volume was observed at T1. Strong positive correlations were observed between dry matter intake (DMI), scrotal circumference, and semen volume. ADG was also strongly correlated with semen volume (r = 0.81), motility (r = 0.78), and scrotal circumference (r = 0.82). The results of this study indicated that concentrate-fed bucks had better daily gain, scrotal development, and functional semen quality traits (semen volume, motility, and concentration) than did range grazing bucks, although the ADG, feed conversion efficiency, and mating frequency of the bucks fed the T3 and T4 diets were similar.

papers.title: Selectivity of acid-base extraction routes and their effects on the structure, physicochemical properties, and adsorption performance of shrimp-shell-derived chitosan.
papers.abstract: Chitosan, obtained from crustacean shells, has broad applications for environmental, agricultural, and pharmaceutical industries. In this study, we synthesized several chitosan samples from shrimp shell waste by applying different combinations of acid and alkali treatments during the demineralization, deproteinization, and deacetylation steps. The degree of deacetylation (DD), determined via titration and attenuated total reflectance-Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR), ranged from 70% to 92%. The physicochemical and structural properties of the extracted chitosan were systematically compared with commercial chitosan (CS-Com) by using X-ray diffraction (XRD), ATR-FTIR, field emission scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (FESEM-EDX), thermogravimetric and differential scanning calorimetry (TGA-DSC), asymmetrical flow field-flow fractionation (AF4), dynamic light scattering (DLS), and Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area analysis. Differences were observed in crystallinity, surface morphology, elemental composition (N/C ratio), porosity, thermal stability, water and fat-binding capacities, solubility, and wettability. Among the samples, CS-2 and CS-5 showed properties most similar to CS-Com. Adsorption studies using chloride and nickel ions as model ions indicated a close relationship between adsorption efficiency and the physicochemical characteristics of chitosan. The acid-base treatment conditions have a major impact on chitosan's solubility, degree of deacetylation, crystallinity, thermal stability, and adsorption performance. The findings provide insights for optimizing chitosan extraction and tailoring the material's properties for biomedical, food, and environmental applications.

papers.title: Intermediate Outcomes of a Randomized Controlled Trial of an Online Group Program to Prevent Dating Violence and Alcohol Use Among Sexual and Gender Minority Teens.
papers.journal: Psychology of sexual orientation and gender diversity
papers.abstract: LGBTQ+ teens are more likely than their heterosexual and cisgender peers to experience teen dating violence (TDV) and engage in substance use. Despite these increased risks, there is a dearth of prevention programming tailored for LGBTQ+ teens. The current study evaluated intermediate outcomes from a pilot randomized controlled trial of an affirming 9-session online group dating violence and alcohol use prevention program for LGBTQ+ teens, the Promoting Resilient Youth with Strong Hearts and Minds (PRYSHM) program. A total of 304 LGBTQ+ teens (ages 15-18) were randomized to complete PRYSHM (n = 213) or to a waitlist (n = 101) between September 2022 and February 2023 and completed surveys at baseline, post-test, and 3-month follow-up. PRYSHM participants were divided into three dosage groups based on number of sessions attended (low 0-2, moderate 3-5, high 6-9), with each group compared to waitlist. As compared to teens assigned to waitlist, teens in the high dosage group (n = 114) had significantly greater sense of LGBTQ+ community (post d = 0.8, 3-month d = 0.5), lower perceived LGBTQ+ peer norms for TDV perpetration (3-month d = 0.4), and greater self-efficacy to engage in alcohol use protective behavioral strategies (post d = 0.3). Results supported that the PRYSHM program led to changes in several proposed intermediate outcomes, but only among teens who received a higher program dose. Given the promise of PRYSHM, future work should evaluate the impact of the program utilizing a longer-term follow-up and consider ways to increase program engagement.

papers.title: Preoptic transcriptomes during courtship reveal the molecular basis of behavioral coordination in a highly social cichlid.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.abstract: Human and non-human animals often coordinate their behavior, a phenomenon thought to strengthen relationships by enabling sequential assessment of an interaction partner's quality as a mate or rival, a process that directly affects evolutionary fitness. There is increasing evidence that behavioral coordination is reflected by synchronized neural activity of the on interacting partners, though few studies have examined synchronization at the level of gene expression. Here, we use Burton's Mouthbrooder cichlid, Astatotilapia burtoni , to examine how neural transcriptomes are synchronized while male-female pairs engaged in variable amounts of reproductive behavior. A. burtoni females naturally display highly coordinated reproductive behavior with a male partner only directly prior to spawning, yet this behavior can be experimentally induced with exogenous prostaglandin F2 alpha (PGF2a), which also acts by releasing pheromones to promote male courtship behavior. We quantified reproductive behavior and circulating sex steroid hormones of PGF2a-treated pairs. We then used transcriptome analysis of the preoptic area - a key node in the regulation of reproductive behavior across vertebrates - and identified gene co-expression modules that showed sex-specific activity in modulating reproductive behavior. Our results, which implement a novel approach to measure transcriptome synchronization, demonstrate a remarkable degree of male-female POA transcriptome synchronization that depends largely on the reproductive responsiveness of the female, mirroring how natural reproduction is driven by female behavior. Together, our work advances our understanding of the molecular mechanisms by which interacting individuals align their actions and how they experience social interaction.

papers.title: A Birth, a Death: The Grief Experiences of Mothers Who Lose One of Their Twins after Birth.
papers.abstract: This study explores the unique grief experiences of mothers who have lost one of their babies after a twin pregnancy. It aims to provide an in-depth understanding of their emotions, the challenges they faced, and their coping strategies. The data were analyzed using six-phase thematic analysis. Data were collected through semi-structured, in-depth interviews with seven mothers in Türkiye who experienced this loss. The analysis revealed that mothers experienced an intense emotional duality characterized by simultaneous grief and attachment to the surviving infant. Mothers described feelings of shock, guilt, emotional conflict, overprotective parenting, and disenfranchised grief shaped by societal minimization of their loss. Interactions with healthcare systems, funeral practices, spouses, and social environments significantly influenced the process. The study highlights the need for trauma-informed psychosocial interventions for bereaved families and emphasizes the importance of legitimizing the grief of mothers who lose one of their twins.

papers.title: Effectiveness of Cognitive Behavioral Couples Therapy on Increasing the Happiness and Marital Satisfaction of Infertile Couples: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Infertility is associated with several psychological problems. Considering the increasing prevalence of infertility and the role of psychological factors, the purpose of this study was to investigate the effectiveness of cognitive behavioral couple therapy on increasing the happiness and marital satisfaction among infertile couples. METHODS: In this randomized controlled trial, 24 infertile couples were selected via convenience sampling from Infertility Center Kermanshah and randomly assigned to cognitive‑behavioral couple therapy (CBCT; 12 couples) or control (routine care; 12 couples). The CBCT group received ten 120‑minute weekly sessions. Data were collected using the Oxford Happiness and ENRICH Marital Satisfaction scales at pre‑test, post‑test, and two‑month follow‑up. Group homogeneity at baseline was assessed using Chi‑square and independent t‑tests. repeated‑measures ANOVA was conducted to evaluate main and interaction effects of group and time on the outcomes. All analyses were performed using SPSS‑25, with significance set at p < 0.05. RESULTS: Repeated‑measures ANOVA revealed significant time × group interaction effects for happiness (F (2,86) = 13.48, p < 0.001, η2 = 0.239) and marital satisfaction (F(2,86) = 16.36, p < 0.001, η2 = 0.276). The CBCT group demonstrated significant improvements in both outcomes from pre‑test to post‑test and follow‑up, while the control group remained stable. CONCLUSIONS: Cognitive Behavioral Couple Therapy can be used in women and in particular infertile men to increasing the happiness and marital satisfaction among them.

papers.title: Golden Oldies and New Top 10: Important Findings and Future Directions for Intimate Partner Violence Research.
papers.abstract: In this brief article, which pays tribute to Langhinrichsen-Rohling's "Top 10 Greatest Hits" review of the intimate partner violence (IPV) literature, the authors comment on progress in 10 key areas and identify directions for future research and practice. These areas include (a) the role of substance use in IPV and the development of integrated IPV-substance use treatment; (b) animal abuse and its implications for shelter policy for women leaving abusive relationships; (c) the finding that coercive control is prevalent and the urgency to define, assess, and understand the impact of nonphysical forms of abuse; (d) the impact of IPV on children and evolving contexts and emerging trends; (e) measurement of psychopathy and its importance to understanding IPV risk; (f) IPV typologies and how they can inform different treatment responses; (g) the mental health effects of experiencing IPV and the need for mental health practitioners' readiness to respond to IPV; (h) IPV in 2SLGBTQQIA+ relationships and its challenges for policing; (i) the finding that justice-involved individuals often do not specialize in IPV and the related prospects for IPV-specific and general violence theory development; (j) measures of IPV recidivism risk and directions for risk communication and violence prevention. The authors describe the contributions of Canadian researchers and international contributions to the IPV literature. They describe the Risk, Need, Responsivity model based on psychological theory that has influenced emerging IPV research, and the co-created RESPECT Framework that guides ethical, equitable, and intersectional collaboration with IPV survivors in future research.

papers.title: The Interplay of Child Sleep Disturbances, Maternal Burnout, and Marital Quality in Iranian Mothers.
papers.abstract: This study examined the relationships between child sleep disturbances, maternal burnout, and marital quality among Iranian mothers. Using a cross-sectional design, data were collected from 564 married mothers of preschool-aged children (aged 5-6 years) through validated questionnaires: the Children's Sleep Habits Questionnaire , the Parental Burnout Assessment , and the Quality of Marriage Index . A structural equation model (SEM) was used to test hypothesized associations among the variables. The final model demonstrated excellent fit to the data. Results indicated a significant positive correlation between child sleep disturbances and maternal burnout ( r  = 0.374, p  < 0.001) and significant negative correlations between maternal burnout and marital quality ( r  = -0.368, p  < 0.001) and between child sleep disturbances and marital quality ( r  = -0.217, p  < 0.001). In the measurement model, strong indicators were identified for each latent variable, including night wakings (β = 0.683) and parasomnias (β = 0.533) for child sleep disturbances, and contrast with the previous maternal self (β = 0.909) and emotional exhaustion (β = 0.864) for maternal burnout. These findings advance theoretical understanding by highlighting key interconnections between child sleep, maternal well-being, and relational outcomes within a specific cultural context. The results underscore the importance of a systemic approach in examining how child sleep disturbances and maternal burnout jointly relate to marital quality, with implications for family well-being interventions.
